transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, I guess what finally pushed me to come in is work. I keep starting things I’m supposed to finish—like the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or the paperwork at the end of the line—and somehow I leave out the last part. And it’s not like I don’t know it matters. I do know. My job kind of depends on those things being done right.

It’s just… I’ll be doing it, and then I’m on to the next thing, or someone says something, or I think I finished it and later realize I didn’t. Sorry, I’m explaining it badly. I work around meat processing, so there are a lot of steps and forms, and it’s not exactly forgiving if you miss something. That’s what’s been freaking me out.
Have you had this kind of trouble finishing tasks and following through since childhood?

Yeah, I think so. My mom actually still has some of my elementary school report cards—she keeps everything, like birthday cards and old permission slips too, which is kind of ridiculous—but around fourth grade, the teachers wrote that I was bright and understood the work, but I needed constant reminders to finish classwork and turn in homework.

I remember that, sort of. Like I’d get what the lesson was about, but if the teacher gave a bunch of instructions, I’d miss pieces unless she was right near me or checking in. It wasn’t that I couldn’t do it, I just… didn’t follow it all the way through unless someone was basically keeping me on track.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

Um… I don’t know if I’d say I worry about lots of different things all the time. I mean, I worry when something is actually going wrong, like at work, because there are real consequences there.

But “many different things” when nothing’s happening… I’m not sure. I guess I’d need to think about what you mean. Like, my brain jumps around a lot, but I don’t know if I’d call all of that worrying.
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep intruding into your mind even when you try to ignore them?

I’m not sure. I mean, I get thoughts stuck in my head sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean by unwanted intrusive thoughts.

Like sometimes a work thing will replay in my head—did I do that step, did I put the form where it goes—but then I’m thinking about the whole line setup and who was working that station that day, and then I’m remembering something totally unrelated, like how my roommate keeps leaving dishes in the sink. Sorry, that’s not really the question.

I don’t think I have, like… a specific thought that keeps forcing its way in when I’m trying to ignore it. At least not that I’ve noticed.
When you’re in the middle of a task, do you get distracted easily?

Yeah. I do. Like, even if I come in at the start of a shift telling myself, okay, today I’m going to stay locked in, I’m going to pay attention to each step… after a while it all kind of blends together.

The cutting, weighing, checking labels—especially the labels, because they all start looking the same after you’ve stared at them long enough—and then I’ll realize I’ve just been looking at the same tray or the log sheet and not really absorbing what I’m supposed to do next. Like my eyes are on it, but my brain is somewhere else.

And then I have to sort of snap myself back and figure out, wait, did I already do this part or was I about to do it? It’s frustrating because I’m trying.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say that’s the main thing I notice. Like at work I’m on my feet a lot anyway, so it’s hard to tell if I’m restless or if I’m just, you know, moving because that’s the job.

If I’m sitting somewhere, I might shift around, but I don’t really think of it as this big feeling like I can’t sit still. Sometimes chairs are just uncomfortable, or I’m thinking about something else, like whether I left my laundry in the washer—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

So… I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed feeling restless in that way.
Have you been feeling down or depressed বেশিরভাগ days?

I’m not sure. I mean, I have days where I feel kind of low or just… off, but I don’t know if I’d call it depressed most days.

Sometimes it depends on the day at work, like if the shift was a mess or people are rushing and then I come home and everything feels heavier than it should. But then other days I’m just tired or annoyed, and I can’t tell if that’s the same thing you mean.

So… I don’t think I’ve been keeping track enough to say “most days” for sure.
Do you find yourself checking the same task over and over because you’re not sure it was done correctly?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, sometimes I look back at something because I get that feeling of, wait, did I actually do that or did I just think about doing it? But I don’t know if I’d say I check it over and over.

At work there are things you’re supposed to double-check anyway, like labels or weights, so it’s hard to tell what’s normal checking and what’s me being unsure. And sometimes someone else comes by and asks about a tray, and then I start thinking about whether I set it in the right spot, and then I remember I also need to text my roommate about groceries—sorry.

So… I guess I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself repeating the same check a bunch of times, not in a way I could clearly point to.
Do these attention problems happen in other parts of your life too, like at home or with chores?

Yeah, it’s not just at work. I mean, work is where it gets me in trouble because I’ll start the sanitation steps or the batch logs or the end-of-line paperwork, and I know I have to finish all of it, but somehow I leave off the last part. Like I’ll think I’m basically done, then later realize I didn’t finish the final piece.

At home it’s kind of the same feeling, like starting chores and not actually getting all the way through them, but the work stuff is what made me come in because that’s… I mean, that’s my job, and I can’t really keep missing the ending of things.
When you lose track of a task, does it usually happen because your mind wanders away from what you’re doing?

Yeah, I think so. Like, I’ll start the shift telling myself, okay, stay locked in, just do one thing at a time. But after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels all kind of blur together, and then I’ll realize I’m just staring at the same tray or the log sheet and I’m not really taking in what I’m supposed to do next.

It’s not always like I’m thinking about something important either. Sometimes my brain just drifts, or it’s like it goes blank for a second. And then I’m behind, or I’m not sure where I was.
Have you been enjoying things less than usual lately?

Um… I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve really been paying attention to that specifically.

Like, I still do things I usually do, I guess. Sometimes I’ll start watching something or scrolling and then somehow I’m looking up, like, meat prices or a recipe or some random thing, but I don’t know if that means I’m enjoying it less or just not staying with it. Sorry, that wasn’t really the question.

I guess I haven’t noticed a big change in enjoying things. I’d have to think about it more.
When you have trouble finishing a task, is it usually because your attention drifts rather than because you feel down?

Yeah, I think it’s more that my attention drifts. Like even when I start the shift really trying to stay locked in, after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels all kind of run together, and then I’ll catch myself just staring at the same tray or the log sheet and not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next.

I don’t think it’s usually because I’m feeling down. It’s more like I lose the thread, and then suddenly I’m like, wait, where was I?
